title: Changing the Rendering Provider or Site on Referrals & Prior Authorizations
content:
Where a Referrals & Prior Authorizations type allows a provider change, a patient may move an open referral to another rendering provider of the same specialty — for imaging and procedures, another site — without a new request; the units and validity carry over. The new provider or site is recorded exactly as listed in the provider or facility directory.

## Conditions

- **Status.** The referral status is submitted or approved when the rendering provider is changed, as the referral record shows it.
- **In-group types.** Where the type requires a Linden Ridge rendering provider, the new provider must be a Linden Ridge clinician.
- **Types that name the provider.** Where the type does not allow a provider change (the HMO Specialist Referral and the Out-of-Network Referral), a different provider needs a new request, because the payer authorizes the named provider.
- **Second opinion.** Where the type allows a second opinion, one second-opinion visit with a different provider of the specialty may be booked against the referral without changing the rendering provider.
- **Site of service.** Where the type restricts the site of service, a visit at a site other than the one on the authorization is not covered by it.
- **Ordered service.** A change of the ordered service itself requires a new request where the type requires one.

## Questions answered

**Do the remaining visits move with the referral when the provider changes?** Yes. On a type that allows the change, the units and the validity dates carry over to the new provider.

**Can the rendering provider be changed on a referral that is still only requested?** No. The status must be submitted or approved at the time of the change.

**Can an In-Group Specialist Referral be moved to a community specialist outside the group?** No. That type requires the rendering provider to be a Linden Ridge clinician.

**Does a second-opinion visit change who the rendering provider is?** No. Where a second opinion is allowed, the one second-opinion visit is booked against the referral and the rendering provider stays as it is.
